project.name: mesh_rag_demo
project.description: Mesh RAG Stage 0: a Flutter dual-target (iOS + Android) demo where two phones each hold a slice of a recipe corpus, meet over BLE/Wi-Fi, and merge their vector index as a Ditto CRDT so on-device RAG queries draw on the peer's tuples after handshake — no WAN required. Uses ditto_live 5.0.0 for P2P sync + DQL persistence and cactus 1.3.0 for on-device embeddings and small-LLM completion, with retrieval implemented as flat-array cosine top-k over the materialized corpus. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: recipe_tuple.dart
nodes.summary: Dart data model for a single recipe document in the Ditto `recipes` collection, with deterministic UUIDv5 seed IDs, Ditto doc serialization helpers, and a copyWith for embedding backfill.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Dart's named-constructor factories (`seed`, `fromDittoValue`) as alternative constructors for different construction paths.

nodes.name: RecipeTuple
nodes.summary: Immutable recipe document with id, dish, contributor, ingredients, steps, embedding, and createdAt; provides UUIDv5-keyed seed factory, Ditto value <-> map round-tripping, copyWith for embedding updates, and a hasEmbedding convenience getter.

nodes.name: dql_queries.dart
nodes.summary: Single-source-of-truth holder for the project's DQL query strings against the Ditto `recipes` collection: selectAll, selectById, upsert (with ON ID CONFLICT DO UPDATE), and setEmbedding.

nodes.name: RecipeQueries
nodes.summary: Static-only constants holder (private constructor) for DQL strings used by DittoService, RetrievalService, and any future sync-verification UI to share identical query text.

nodes.name: recipe_merge.dart
nodes.summary: Prompt builder for the on-device LLM merge step: assembles a system message asking cactus to synthesize one coherent recipe from K retrieved variants and a user message enumerating each variant's contributor, ingredients, and steps.

nodes.name: RecipeMergePrompt
nodes.summary: Static prompt-builder class with private constructor; `build(query, retrieved)` returns a List<ChatMessage> pairing the careful-home-cook system instruction with a structured user message enumerating variants for cactus_complete to merge.

nodes.name: cactus_service.dart
nodes.summary: Singleton wrapper around the Cactus on-device LLM that exposes embedding generation and streaming/non-streaming chat completion for the RAG pipeline. Pins model slugs at compile time for demo-day reproducibility.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a private named constructor + static `instance` field for the Dart idiom of a manually-managed singleton.

nodes.name: CactusService
nodes.summary: Owns the Cactus LLM lifecycle: model download/initialization, embedding generation, and streaming chat completion. Stage 0 reuses a single qwen3-0.6 slug for both embed and complete to stay under the first-launch download budget.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Downloads (if needed) and initializes the Cactus model with a progress callback, idempotent on repeat calls.

nodes.name: complete
nodes.summary: Async generator that streams completion token chunks from the Cactus model for a given chat-message history.

nodes.name: ditto_service.dart
nodes.summary: Singleton that owns the Ditto CRDT runtime: init with offline license, small-peers-only transport (BLE + LAN + AWDL), presence stream, and DQL CRUD over `RecipeTuple`. Backbone of the mesh sync layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Configuration is injected at compile time via `String.fromEnvironment` (Flutter's `--dart-define`).

nodes.name: DittoService
nodes.summary: Manages the global Ditto instance: initialization with offline license, peer-to-peer transport config, presence broadcasting, and RecipeTuple CRUD via DQL. Dart-side filters embeddings rather than using DQL predicates to dodge MISSING/NULL ambiguity.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Opens a Ditto instance with the injected app id + offline license, enables BLE/LAN/AWDL transports, and wires the presence observer that drives the peer-count stream.

nodes.name: subscribeToRecipes
nodes.summary: Registers a live store observer that fires the supplied callback whenever a RecipeTuple is added, modified, or removed (locally or via mesh sync).

nodes.name: retrieval_service.dart
nodes.summary: Stage 0 RAG core: embeds missing recipes back into Ditto, runs brute-force cosine top-k over the merged corpus, and streams the answer pipeline as an `AnswerEvent` discriminated union.
nodes.languageNotes: Brute force is deliberate: ≤5k tuples × 384 dims fits in <8MB so an index would just be CRDT merge overhead with no recall win.

nodes.name: RetrievalService
nodes.summary: Coordinates the RAG loop end-to-end: ensures embeddings exist in Ditto, embeds the user query, runs cosine top-k, builds the merge prompt, and streams completion tokens. Exposes static `normalize`/`dot` helpers for testing.

nodes.name: RetrievedRecipe
nodes.summary: Immutable value object pairing a RecipeTuple with its cosine similarity score against the query.

nodes.name: AnswerEvent
nodes.summary: Discriminated union over the events the answer pipeline emits: a retrieved-results frame, a streaming token, or a done marker. Lets the UI render attribution before the LLM finishes.

nodes.name: topK
nodes.summary: Computes cosine top-k against the embedded portion of the Ditto corpus, normalizing both query and doc vectors so the score stays in [-1, 1].

nodes.name: answerQuery
nodes.summary: Async-generator end-to-end pipeline: embed query, run topK, yield retrieved frame, build the merge prompt, and yield streaming token events until done.

nodes.name: ensureEmbeddings
nodes.summary: Embeds every recipe row missing an embedding and writes the vector back to Ditto so the CRDT can sync it to peers. Idempotent.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Returns the L2-normalized copy of a Float32List (identity on a zero vector). Pure math, unit tested.

nodes.name: seed_loader.dart
nodes.summary: Loads role-specific seed recipes from a bundled JSON asset (selected via `--dart-define=PHONE_ROLE=a|b`) and upserts each into Ditto, with idempotency guaranteed by the deterministic seed UUID.

nodes.name: SeedLoader
nodes.summary: Singleton that resolves the device's role (phone-a or phone-b), loads the matching JSON asset, and inserts each recipe into Ditto. Exposes `selfContributor` so the UI can count peer-vs-local tuples.

nodes.name: mesh_status_widget.dart

nodes.name: MeshStatusWidget
nodes.summary: StatefulWidget that displays current peer count with color-coded connection state. Listens on DittoService.peerCount in its State and rebuilds on changes.

nodes.name: query_screen.dart
nodes.summary: The Stage-0 demo screen: text input, streaming answer pane, mesh-status pill, and a '(N tuples, M from peers)' attribution footer. Wires the RetrievalService AnswerEvent stream into UI state.

nodes.name: QueryScreen
nodes.summary: StatefulWidget hosting the demo's single screen — query input, streaming answer, and peer-attribution footer.

tour.title: The Thesis
tour.description: Begin where the project began. SEED.md is the Software-Factory seed document that names the wager — that a vector index can sync as a CRDT and make WAN-free, peer-to-peer RAG real — while README.md translates that thesis into the actual Stage 0 stack (Flutter dual-target, ditto_live 5.0.0 for sync, cactus 1.3.0 narrowly scoped to embeddings + completion). Read these together to understand what the demo is trying to prove before looking at how it proves it.

tour.title: The Plan That Drove The Build
tour.description: Between thesis and code sits the implementation plan. The Stage 0 plan enumerates the U1–U10 work units (scaffold, determinism spike, recipe-merge eval, retrieval, sync verification, demo rehearsal) that shaped every file you are about to read. pubspec.yaml is the receipt — it pins exactly the dependencies the plan called for and bundles the per-phone seed_recipes_{a,b}.json assets that make the corpus-split demo possible.

tour.title: App Boot Lifecycle
tour.description: lib/main.dart is the Flutter entry point and the choreographer of the entire boot sequence. It requests BLE and Wi-Fi runtime permissions, then runs MeshRagApp whose BootScreen orchestrates a strict order: Ditto init → seed insert → Cactus model download → embedding backfill → swap in the QueryScreen. This file is the load-bearing scaffold; every later step is something this file imports.
tour.languageLesson: Dart async/await with Flutter: top-level `main()` is async, calls `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` before any plugin work, and BootScreen uses a StatefulWidget with sequential `await` calls inside `initState`-triggered futures to keep startup deterministic across iOS and Android.

tour.title: Data Model & Sync Layer
tour.description: The data layer is where the CRDT promise becomes concrete. RecipeTuple is the immutable Dart record that round-trips through Ditto's DQL store. ditto_service.dart (fan-in 11 — the most depended-upon file in the project) owns Ditto identity, transport config, store registration, and the insert/observe paths. dql_queries.dart centralizes every DQL string so the rest of the codebase never hand-rolls a query. seed_loader.dart reads the per-phone JSON asset and inserts it into Ditto so each device starts the demo holding only its slice of the corpus.
tour.languageLesson: DQL (Ditto Query Language) is a SQL-like surface over a CRDT document store. Queries return live result sets you `observe()` for changes, and inserts are local-first — they replicate to peers as they appear without a central coordinator.

tour.title: On-Device Retrieval
tour.description: With tuples flowing through the CRDT, retrieval happens entirely on-device. CactusService is held deliberately narrow: it exposes only `embed()` and `complete()`, never cactus_rag_query or cactus_index_*, because the project's thesis is that the *index* lives in Ditto, not Cactus. RetrievalService materializes the merged corpus out of Ditto, runs a flat-array cosine top-k in Dart, and returns the nearest tuples — including tuples that arrived from the peer over BLE.
tour.languageLesson: Flat-array cosine top-k is intentionally chosen over HNSW/Annoy/FAISS for Stage 0: with a few hundred recipe tuples per device, an O(N) scan in Dart is faster end-to-end than building and merging an ANN index, and — critically — it has no index data structure that would need its own CRDT merge semantics.

tour.title: Synthesis & Attribution
tour.description: Retrieval returns tuples; synthesis turns them into an answer. RecipeMergePrompt builds the system+user message that asks the on-device LLM to merge retrieved recipes while tagging each contributor — so when phone A answers a query using tuples that came from phone B, the provenance is visible in the output. RetrievalService.answerQuery threads the embedding, top-k, prompt-building, and Cactus completion into a single call the UI can await.

tour.title: User Interface & Mesh Status
tour.description: QueryScreen is the post-boot UI: a text field, a result panel, and a continuous mesh-status indicator. MeshStatusWidget subscribes to Ditto's peer-presence stream so the demo audience can watch the peer connect over BLE/Wi-Fi in real time — making the otherwise-invisible CRDT merge legible. Together these widgets close the loop from the boot lifecycle in Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: Flutter StreamBuilder pattern: MeshStatusWidget wraps a `StreamBuilder<List<Peer>>` over the Ditto presence stream, rebuilding only the status chip on peer-list changes — idiomatic Flutter for live, push-based UI without manual setState plumbing.

tour.title: Verification Surface
tour.description: Trust in the demo comes from two layers of verification. The Dart unit tests pin the contracts that matter most — RecipeTuple parsing round-trips, retrieval ranks deterministically, and RecipeMergePrompt produces the exact system+user shape (including the graceful 'I don't know yet' fallback for empty retrieval). The U7 spike then proves the harder claim: that two physical phones actually mesh over BLE/LAN and that tuples inserted on A become queryable on B.

tour.title: The Deliverables
tour.description: Stage 0 is a demo first and a codebase second. slides/deck.md is the ~10-minute Presenterm deck that frames the thesis (vector index as CRDT) for an audience, and slides/notes.md is the per-slide speaker-notes script with timing budgets and framing reminders. These are the artifacts that translate everything in Steps 1–8 into a story a viewer can follow in a single sitting.
tour.languageLesson: Presenterm is a terminal-based Markdown deck tool: slides are plain Markdown separated by `---`, rendered live in the terminal with syntax-highlighted code blocks. The format keeps decks diff-friendly in git and avoids the GUI tooling that usually surrounds conference slides.

tour.title: Future-Work Arc
tour.description: Close on the questions Stage 0 deliberately did not answer. open-questions.md catalogues the empirical work that follows: Cactus iOS/Android determinism parity, larger corpora, richer merge semantics, and the leap from this generalist-on-device demo to the specialist-small-model destination the broader Mesh RAG thesis points toward. This is the bridge from 'we proved it can work' to 'here is what it could become'.
